1:3.arabic: رواه عن النبي ﭬ أنه قال: (إن الله تعالى يمجد نفسه كل يوم ويقول إني أنا الله رب العالمين إني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا الحي القيوم... مالك يوم الدين خالق الخير والشر خالق الجنة والنار...
1:3.english: Al-Ghazali records a powerful supplication (dua) demonstrating that when turning to Allah, one must acknowledge Him deeply in the heart as the Creator of all good and evil, the One and Only Sovereign over the seen and unseen. Reaffirming these Divine Names—especially as the Master of the Day of Judgment—is the ultimate path to having one's prayers answered and attaining true spiritual purification.

2:127.arabic: وتقول عند التصدق ﴿ ربنا تقبل منا إنك أنت السميع العليم ﴾
2:127.english: Al-Ghazali highlights the etiquette of relying on Allah in all states. Just as the Prophets built the Kaaba with the plea for acceptance, the believer is instructed to recite 'Our Lord, accept from us' specifically when giving charity. This ensures the act is stripped of ego, purifying the intention so that the deed is presented entirely for the sake of God alone.

2:128.arabic: اللهم املأ وجوهنا منك حياء وقلوبنا منك فرقا واسكن في نفوسنا من عظمتك ما تذلل به جوارحنا لخدمتك. واجعلك اللهم أحب إلينا ممن سواك واجعلنا أخشى لك ممن سواك
2:128.english: Drawing upon the spirit of submitting absolutely to Allah's will, Al-Ghazali presents profound supplications focusing on deep inner reverence (khushu'). True submission is achieved by begging Allah to fill our hearts with awe, to make Him more beloved and feared than anything else, and to grant us the ultimate spiritual success of sincere alignment with His Divine Reality.
